details: The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, reportedly climbed above 4% in May 2026, marking a three-year high. Consumer prices also rose 4.1% annually, largely driven by higher energy prices and demand for semiconductors. This persistent inflationary pressure has reignited fears of further interest rate hikes, impacting Wall Street and broader financial markets.
sourceName: AP News (as reported by America In Focus)
title: US Inflation Surges to 3-Year High in May, Reigniting Rate Hike Fears

details: A recent Reuters poll of economists indicates a significant shift in expectations, with the consensus now predicting no Federal Reserve interest rate cuts until 2028. This marks a complete reversal from projections made earlier in June 2026. The change in outlook suggests a prolonged period of higher interest rates, impacting liquidity and investor sentiment across global markets.
sourceName: Reuters (as referenced by Binance Market Update)
title: Economists Expect No Fed Rate Cuts Until 2028, Reversing Earlier Projections

details: Bitcoin has been struggling to maintain the psychologically critical $60,000 threshold, briefly dipping below it. The cryptocurrency market is showing high sensitivity to Federal Reserve rate expectations and has seen weak performance in spot Bitcoin ETF flows, with a series of withdrawals observed. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index is currently at 15, signaling "Extreme Fear" among investors. This suggests a sustained absence of net new demand for Bitcoin at the base layer.
sourceName: Sergey Tereshkin (via personal blog/platform), Intellectia.AI, MEXC
title: Bitcoin Struggles Below $60,000 Amid Weak ETF Flows and Macro Headwinds

details: On June 11, 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) raised its three key interest rates by 25 basis points, making it the first rate hike since September 2023. The decision was made to combat inflation, which is now projected to average 3.0% in the euro area for 2026, primarily due to inflation pressures stemming from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The ECB's latest Economic Bulletin, published June 25, 2026, reiterates this stance and revised inflation forecasts upwards for 2026 and 2027, while revising growth forecasts downwards.
title: ECB Raises Interest Rates by 25 Basis Points Amid Rising Inflation

details: Escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and its impact on the Strait of Hormuz, continue to disrupt global oil transportation and supply chains. These disruptions have led to increased energy prices and heightened volatility across global financial markets. While some diplomatic efforts have eased immediate concerns, the potential for renewed conflict remains a significant risk, influencing investor sentiment and contributing to inflationary pressures worldwide.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Continue to Drive Energy Price Volatility and Market Uncertainty
